name: Marketing attribution
stages: Channel reporting — ad-spend exports + order exports → spreadsheet reconciliation by date/channel → descriptive spend and sales report. No customer-level attribution is implied.
Joined attribution reporting — ad clicks/UTMs + consented sessions + orders → connector ingestion, deduplication and identity rules → attributable conversions with unmatched orders shown.
Attribution comparison — joined touchpoints + orders → a semantic layer applies explicit attribution windows/models → compare credited revenue and acquisition cost. Attribution is not causal lift.

Incrementality analysis — valid experiment or holdout data + campaign exposure + outcomes → experiment analysis with uncertainty → evidence for incremental contribution; observational data alone is insufficient.

name: Campaign budget planning
stages: Budget pacing — campaign budgets + current spend → scheduled aggregation and rules → under/overspend alerts for the marketer.
Performance diagnosis — campaign spend + orders + product margins → joined metrics and anomaly analysis → investigate changes in acquisition efficiency.
Budget simulation — historical spend/outcomes + seasonality + business constraints → validated response models and explicit assumptions → compare allocation scenarios, not guaranteed ROAS.

Reviewed budget recommendations — scenario results + stock/margin constraints → explainable recommendation and approval queue → marketer approves a supported change; write-back API and permissions must be verified.

name: Inventory planning and replenishment
stages: Stock reporting — SKU/location stock + receipts + sales + returns → spreadsheet or batch reconciliation → stock-on-hand report.
Inventory visibility — authorised inventory/WMS feeds + sales feeds → connector ingestion and shared SKU/location IDs → stock movement and availability dashboard.
Inventory diagnosis — stock history + demand + lead times → exception rules and analytical joins → identify stockout, ageing-stock and excess-stock drivers.
Demand forecasting — relevant SKU/location sales history + promotions + availability → validated forecasting models with uncertainty → demand estimates; account for stockout-censored sales.

Replenishment simulation — demand estimates + available/open-order stock + lead times + minimum order quantities → constrained planning model → compare reorder quantities, timing and safety-stock scenarios.
Reviewed replenishment — proposed orders + cash/service-level constraints → human approval and audit workflow → an approved plan; purchase-order execution requires a supported external API.
Outcome monitoring — actual demand + deliveries + stock outcomes → forecast-error and inventory-performance tracking → planners revise models and replenishment rules.

name: Customer retention planning
stages: Cohort reporting — orders + consented customer identifiers → cohort aggregation → observed repeat-purchase rate and time to second order.
Lifecycle diagnosis — order cohorts + CRM engagement + cancellation/return signals → governed joins and segment comparisons → identify where repeat purchasing weakens.
Retention prediction — sufficient historical behaviour and outcomes → validated churn/next-purchase models → risk estimates with uncertainty; not assumed available from an LLM alone.
Intervention experiments — eligible consented segments + model outputs + campaign rules → reviewed audience proposals and controlled tests → assess retention interventions before expanding them.

name: Product assortment and merchandising
stages: Product reporting — orders + variants + refunds → product-level aggregation → best/worst sellers by units, revenue and returns.
Conversion diagnosis — product/session/cart events + orders + availability → funnel and stock-aware analysis → identify where product journeys lose demand.
Assortment analysis — baskets + margins + inventory + product attributes → co-purchase and catalogue analysis → bundle or range hypotheses, not proof of causal impact.
Merchandising simulation — historical outcomes + proposed range/price changes + explicit assumptions → scenario models → compare possible margin and demand effects.

Reviewed experiments — scenario hypotheses + business constraints → experiment design and approved publishing workflow → measure actual results; storefront write-back is optional and must be verified.

name: Contribution margin and profitability analysis
stages: Revenue reporting — orders + refunds → consistent aggregation → net sales by period/product/channel.
Contribution calculation — sales + product costs + ad spend + fulfilment/payment fees → reconciled cost joins and agreed definitions → contribution views with missing costs flagged.
Profitability diagnosis — contribution data + cohorts + channels + product mix → variance analysis → explain changes in observed profitability without inventing costs.

Cash and margin scenarios — demand assumptions + unit economics + inventory commitments → finance-reviewed scenario model → compare economic consequences; management estimates are not booked accounting results.
